items.title: Lesson Podcast
items.description: Audio guide to Gibson's direct theory — optic flow, affordances and why he argued the world provides enough information to perceive without inference.

items.title: All in the Mind — BBC Radio 4
items.description: Radio 4 programme on visual processing that debates bottom-up versus top-down perception — directly relevant to Gibson's position.

items.title: Gibson's Direct Theory SHORT — AQA GCSE Psychology
items.description: Concise AQA-focused revision video covering optic flow, affordances and the visual cliff as evidence for direct perception.

items.title: You Don't See Objects, You See Opportunities: The Theory of Affordances
items.description: Explores Gibson's affordance concept in depth — how the environment directly offers action possibilities without mental inference.

items.title: Gibson — Visual Cliff Experiments (Affordances) — 1960s
items.description: Footage and discussion of the visual cliff experiment, which Gibson and Walk used as evidence for innate direct depth perception.

items.title: Fantastic Voyage
items.description: Classic sci-fi about miniaturised scientists navigating the human body — a creative visual companion to thinking about how our perceptual system processes the environment.

items.title: Simply Psychology — Visual Perception Theory
items.description: Covers Gibson's direct (bottom-up) theory alongside Gregory's constructivist theory for comparison — key revision material.

items.title: AQA GCSE Psychology 8182 — Specification
items.description: Official specification listing Gibson's theory content and the depth cues you are assessed on.
